doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

title: Touring overseas and audiences
summary: He toured Japan, Europe and New Zealand annually and finds jazz audiences universal.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Have you been overseas on tours playing jazz?
Oh for years. I mean that’s when I said going on tour, you know, in the last 26 years I was going to Japan, Europe, New Zealand, annually I was going all over the place.
Was there a noticeable difference in the audience reaction in general?

Oh I think in a city like New York or Los Angeles, you know it’s possible to encounter an audience that might be a little more blasé, but I have never experienced that. The audiences here are great. People really want to hear the music, they want to be a part of the music. Overseas obviously if you’re someone coming from out of the country to visit and as someone that they all know from a record or a video or something, that might add
a little more draw power or maybe a little more celebrity to what you’re doing, but I find jazz audiences to be pretty universal.
